  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  C. AUTHORIZE RADIO PURCHASE IN THE AMOUNT OF $67,518 FROM
  MOTOROLA SOLUTIONS UNDER 2020 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY
  GRANT PROGRAM

  The San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) was awarded a grant from the 2020
  State Homeland Security Program (SHSP) in the amount of $67,518. The
  department is seeking to utilize this funding towards the purchase of (5) five
  new Motorola APX 8000 portable radios, and (3) three new Motorola APX 8500
  mobile radios to enhance communications at SGPD and interoperability with
  other police agencies within the Los Angeles County region. This program does
  not require matching funds from the City and there is no impact to the City’s
  General Fund.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council wave formal bidding to purchase the items from
  Motorola Solutions pursuant to Municipal Code Section 34.35 and authorize
  the Police Chief to authorize the purchase of the Motorola equipment using the
  allocated State Homeland Security Program grant funding.

  D. RATIFICATION OF THE LEASE AGREEMENT WITH THE BUSINESS KNOWN
  AS LUNAS BAR AND GRILL LOCATED AT 343 SOUTH MISSION DRIVE

  On August 1, 2021, the City entered into a new agreement to lease City owned
  property located at 343 South Mission Drive. The lessee intended in leasing the
  existing commercial building and continue operating the business known as
  Luna’s Mexican Restaurant. Prior to entering this new lease, the City maintained
  a long-term lease for the same property with operator, Efrain Avila Martinez for
  the same business. New lessee/business owner, Roxane Enterprises, Limited
  Liability Company took over the lease on August 1, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 4, 2022  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the new agreement, and
  authorize the City Manager to execute it, in effect also ratifying the prior
  agreement.

  E. SMALL BUSINESS ASSISTANCE PROGRAM RECAP

  Earlier this year, the City launched the Small Business Assistance Program
  (Program), which provided grants of up to $2,500 to small businesses. The
  Program utilized American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding and was mirrored
  after a Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) business assistance grant
  program from the previous year. From April 1, 2022 until May 1, 2022, the City
  received applications from 68 businesses, of which 58 were eligible for funding.
  Recently, staff surveyed the grant recipients to gather feedback on the Program.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file this report.

  F. APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. 22-61 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE OFFICER’S
  ASSOCIATION FOR THE JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 PERIOD
  AND INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR POLICE
  OFFICER SALARIES

  On May 5, 2022, the City and San Gabriel Police Officer’s Association (POA)
  entered negotiations for a successor Memorandum of Understanding (MOU).
  The most recent MOU between the City and POA expired on June 30, 2022.
  Representatives of the City and POA have reached an agreement on a three-
  year successor MOU for the July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025 period. The
  three-year successor MOU with the POA is expected to have a total three-year
  cost impact of $1,969,281.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 22-61, which
  ratifies the three-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2022
  through June 30, 2025 between the City and POA and appropriates $454,672 in
  General Funds for increased Police Officer salaries, and authorize City’s
  negotiators to execute the MOU.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 4, 2022  4
   G. APPROVING RESOLUTION NO. 22-62 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL FIREFIGHTER’S ASSOCIATION
  FOR THE JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 PERIOD AND
  INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR FIRE PERSONNEL
  SALARIES

  On May 9, 2022, the City and San Gabriel Firefighter’s Association (FFA) entered
  negotiations for a successor Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). The most
  recent MOU between the City and FFA expired on June 30, 2022.
  Representatives of the City and FFA have reached an agreement on a three-
  year successor MOU for the July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025 period. The
  three-year successor MOU with the FFA is expected to have a total three-year
  cost impact of $2,428,634.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 22-62, which
  ratifies the three-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2022
  through June 30, 2025 between the City and FFA and appropriates $572,999 in
  General Funds for increased Fire Department salaries, and authorize City’s
  negotiators to execute the MOU.

  H. JOINT EXERCISE OF POWERS AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL
  VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS TO JOIN THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  REGIONAL HOUSING TRUST

  The San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust (SGRVHT) is a Joint Powers
  Authority (JPA) which allows member agencies in the San Gabriel Valley to bring
  affordable housing resources to the region. The SGVRHT is governed by a nine-
  member Board of Directors and receives public and private financing and funds
  to support these projects throughout the San Gabriel Valley region. A specific
  SGVRHT funding source for member agencies is the Revolving Loan Fund (RLF)
  which has $8 million (from the $20 million earmark from the State budget) to
  support projects in earlier stages with predevelopment loans. The City is
  currently an affiliate member of the SGVRHT, however full membership in the
  JPA would allow the City access to the funding and technical assistance
  opportunities, including the RLF, for affordable housing projects such as 405
  South Del Mar Avenue. The current year annual full member fee is $15,210.68,
  which will increase by Consumer Price Index (CPI) each year. For this year,
  LACDA is willing to pay half of the membership fee which reduce costs to the
  City to $7,605.34.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 4, 2022  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the City’s full membership in
  the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust so that the City may have access
  to the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust funding and technical
  assistance opportunities for affordable housing projects such as 405 South Del
  Mar Avenue, and authorize the execution of the Joint Powers agreement.
